items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I took a gig at a record company, in fact Joe Muranyi was here and it was the same company, it was the RCA Victor Company.

ctx.x: I took a gig at a record company, in fact Joe Muranyi was here and it was the same company, it was the RCA Victor Company. And it was, in my time, known as BMG. Burtlesman Music Company. And I worked in the archive, which was a wonderful gig. And I had kind of had enough. I tried to run everything by myself, it’s really hard.

items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: Tim Hicks and Vince Giordano participated briefly in the interview.

ctx.x: He has worked as a record producer for major labels and played alongside Roy Eldridge, Jimmy McPartland and Max Kaminsky. Joe was a member of the Louis Armstrong All-Stars from 1967-1971.
Joe was interviewed in New York City on January 11, 2007 by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. Tim Hicks and Vince Giordano participated briefly in the interview.
My name is Monk Rowe and we’re in Manhattan at the International Association of Jazz Educators conference. I’m pleased to have Joe Muranyi with me this afternoon. Did I pronounce your name good?
